title: Four Messages, Left Out of Order
gist_ar: أربع رسايل على الرد الآلي، مش مرتّبة زمنيًا. لازم ترتّبها وتستنتج اللي حصل.

before_listening.en: Four voicemails played back in the order they were left, which is not the order the events happened. Work out the sequence.
before_listening.ar: أربع رسايل صوتية بترتيب تركها، وهو مش ترتيب الأحداث. رتّب الأحداث بنفسك.

segments.speaker: Message one — Hala
segments.text: Hi, it's Hala, it's about ten past nine on the Tuesday. Look, ignore my last one, I'd got it completely the wrong way round. The valuation didn't come in low, the valuation came in fine — it's the survey that's flagged the retaining wall at the back. So the number in the email is right, the reason is wrong. I've asked Marwan to send you the survey itself rather than his summary of it, because his summary says 'movement noted' and the actual survey says 'no evidence of recent movement', and those are quite different sentences to be making a decision on. Ring me.

segments.speaker: Message two — Marwan
segments.text: It's Marwan, Tuesday about half eleven. Hala's told me off, entirely fairly. I've sent the full survey. Page fourteen is the wall. What it says is the crack is historic, it's been pointed at some stage, and the surveyor's recommendation is monitoring rather than works. So the eight thousand in my summary was my own estimate for rebuilding it, which I shouldn't have put in a document without labelling it as mine. There's no eight thousand anywhere in the survey. Sorry. Genuinely.

segments.speaker: Message three — Hala
segments.text: Me again, Tuesday, just gone two. Right, so the seller has come back and they'll do monitoring at their cost for twelve months, in writing, and they want an answer by Friday because there's a second party. I have no way of telling you whether the second party is real. In my experience it's real about half the time. What I can tell you is that the monitoring offer is unusual and it's worth more than the eight thousand you were braced for, because it transfers the uncertainty to them. Friday, then. And don't ring Marwan about the valuation, he's had enough.

segments.speaker: Message four — Nadia
segments.text: It's your sister. It's Wednesday morning. I've had all three of them forwarded to me and I want to say one thing and then I'll leave you alone. Everyone in those messages is talking about the wall. Nobody is talking about the fact that you told me in January you didn't want to live that far from Baba, and the wall is the thing you've found to be worried about instead. That may be completely unfair. If it is, ignore me and buy the house, and I'll help you paint it. But if I'm right, you've got until Friday and a retaining wall is a much easier conversation than the real one, so I thought somebody should say the real one out loud.

gist_question.q: What is the actual state of the retaining wall?
options: It needs rebuilding at a cost of eight thousand
The valuation has come in low because of it
There is a historic crack with no recent movement; the surveyor recommends monitoring
The survey found evidence of recent movement

questions.q: Where did the figure of eight thousand actually come from?
options: The surveyor's recommendation on page fourteen
Marwan's own unlabelled estimate for rebuilding, not the survey
The seller's opening offer
The valuation report
Eight thousand off the asking price
Monitoring at their own cost for twelve months, in writing
To rebuild the wall before completion
A second survey by a different firm

questions.q: What does Hala correct in her first message?
options: That the deadline is Friday, not Thursday
That Marwan is no longer acting on the sale
That the survey, not the valuation, is the source of the problem
That the wall is at the front, not the back

questions.q: What does Nadia argue in the last message?
options: That the wall may be a substitute worry for not wanting to live far from their father
That the second party is unlikely to be real
That the survey should be redone before Friday
That Marwan has behaved unprofessionally and should be replaced

questions.q: Why does Hala say the monitoring offer is worth more than eight thousand?
options: Because monitoring costs more than eight thousand over twelve months
Because it removes the need for a survey
Because the second party has offered less
Because it shifts the uncertainty onto the seller
